This subject pins my own verdict on g30-input-corpus.v1 — a file I wrote earlier today and then corrected, having found my attacksRunCount reading 26 against a 27-element array. A digest match alone would not tell you which version was captured, so I opened the pinned file: it reads 27/27, so the pin holds the corrected bytes, and the file has since been frozen from 644 to 0444. More importantly the successor is additive in the strict sense: four of five inherited obligations are byte-identical to v1, the fifth changes only prose with its flag unchanged at TRUE, and summary.leftoverDesign is == v1's single element. Adding an obligation at false is precisely how a successor could quietly shrink a leftover set, and the arithmetic shows it did not. On the version-collision finding, both limbs are clean — artifact and version both say 2, and I searched v1's own roles and found no version claim, since v1 is first in the family and has no predecessor roles. Notably v2 carries no findingDisposition and does not name the finding, stating compliance in the predecessor role instead; that is the honest form here, because the sibling structure that lands this finding explicitly would have claimed a repair that never happened. The token is DR-G30's own cell [7] OPEN, corroborated by live G30 v1's liveStatusVerbatim and by the accepted predecessor. The named corpus string is an exact substring of live liveHarnessCellVerbatim and of the live register cell [2], attributed to liveHarnessCellVerbatim by name. The EE census is 7a, 7b and 7d at 15 each with EE-7c correctly absent. All seventeen cited digests match, partition is exact at six obligations, the bare-integer set is 2, 5, 08 and 26, and neither the subject nor v1 moved. Twenty-eight attacks run, twenty-eight refuted, zero findings. One note for a coordinator: the subject's top-level namedCorpusNotAuthored holds the one-string harness-cell phrase while live G30 v1's field of the same name holds three class names — nothing false, since the obligation attributes the string to liveHarnessCellVerbatim and it is exact there, but a check comparing same-named fields across the two artifacts would report a mismatch that is not one.
